title: Data binding and events
summary: @bind, @onclick, EventCallback, and when the UI re-renders.

predict.title: One-way value
options: An error: `value` can't be set from C#
predict.explanation: **Hello, Ana!** `value="@name"` is **one-way**: it writes `name` into the input, but nothing listens to the input's events, so the field never changes. The box shows **Bo**, the field is still **Ana**. Use `@bind="name"` for two-way binding.

predict.title: Default bind event
options: City: Rome, updated after each key
predict.explanation: `@bind` on an input updates the field on **`onchange`**, which fires when the input **loses focus** (or on Enter). While the user is still typing, `city` is still empty. After Tab, it shows **City: Rome**. Add `@bind:event="oninput"` to update on every key.

predict.title: Action instead of EventCallback
options: An error: a lambda can't be passed to a parameter
Count: 2, because the child and the page both re-render
predict.explanation: **Count: 0.** The lambda runs and `count` becomes 1, but the event happened in the **child**, so only the child re-renders. A plain `Action` doesn't tell the page to render. Change the parameter to **`EventCallback`** and call `OnAdd.InvokeAsync()`: then Blazor re-renders the page automatically, and it shows **Count: 1**.

predict.title: An async handler
predict.explanation: For an `async Task` handler, Blazor re-renders when the handler **first awaits** (so **Loading...** shows) and **again when the task completes** (so **Done** shows). No `StateHasChanged()` is needed. With `async void`, Blazor couldn't wait for the end, and the second render would be missing.

practice.title: Make it two-way
practice.task:
Typing in this input doesn't update the greeting. Fix it:

1. Bind the input to **`name`** in **both** directions.
2. Update `name` on **every key**, not when the input loses focus.
practice.hint: Replace `value="@name"` with `@bind`, then choose the event with `@bind:event`.

checks.label: The one-way `value="@name"` is gone
checks.hint: Remove `value="@name"`: `@bind` sets the value for you.

practice.title: Wire up the buttons
practice.task:
Add click handlers:

1. **+1** calls the method **`Increment`** (pass the method itself, no parentheses).
2. **+5** calls **`Add(5)`** with a **lambda**.
3. Write `Increment`, which adds 1 to `count`.
practice.starter:
Count: @count

@code { private int count; private void Add(int n) => count += n; }
practice.solution:
Count: @count

@code { private int count; private void Increment() => count++; private void Add(int n) => count += n; }
practice.hint: A method group is `@onclick="Increment"`. A lambda is `@onclick="() => Add(5)"`.

checks.label: No call during render (`@onclick="Increment()"`)
checks.hint: Remove the parentheses: pass `Increment`, don't call it.

practice.title: Fix the double onchange
practice.task:
An AI tool wrote this search box. It doesn't build, because `@bind` already uses `onchange`.

Fix it:

1. Keep `@bind="search"`, and update on every key.
2. Run **`Filter`** after the value changes, with **`@bind:after`**.
3. Remove `@onchange`.
practice.starter:
@results.Count results

@code { private string search = ""; private List results = []; private void Filter() { results = AllNames.Where(n => n.Contains(search)).ToList(); } }
practice.solution:
@results.Count results

@code { private string search = ""; private List results = []; private void Filter() { results = AllNames.Where(n => n.Contains(search)).ToList(); } }

checks.label: No `@onchange` on the input
checks.hint: Remove `@onchange="Filter"`: `@bind` and `@onchange` can't share an element.

practice.title: Press Enter to add
practice.task:
Add an item when the user presses **Enter** in the input:

1. Add **`@onkeydown="OnKeyDown"`** to the input.
2. Write **`OnKeyDown`** with a **`KeyboardEventArgs`** parameter.
3. If the key is **`"Enter"`**, call `Add()`.
practice.starter:
@foreach (var item in items) {
  • @item
    • }
@code { private string newItem = ""; private List items = []; private void Add() { items.Add(newItem); newItem = ""; } }
practice.solution:
@foreach (var item in items) {
  • @item
    • }
@code { private string newItem = ""; private List items = []; private void OnKeyDown(KeyboardEventArgs e) { if (e.Key == "Enter") { Add(); } } private void Add() { items.Add(newItem); newItem = ""; } }
practice.hint: Inside the handler, `e.Key` holds the key name, like `"Enter"`.

checks.label: It calls `Add()`
checks.hint: Call `Add();` inside `OnKeyDown` when the key is Enter.

practice.title: Make the stepper bindable
practice.task:
The page wants to write `<Stepper @bind-Value="quantity" />`. Right now the stepper changes its own parameter. Fix it:

1. Add a parameter **`ValueChanged`** of type **`EventCallback<int>`**.
2. The buttons call **`Change(1)`** and **`Change(-1)`**.
3. `Change` sends `Value + delta` to the parent with **`ValueChanged.InvokeAsync`**.
4. Never assign `Value` inside the component.
practice.hint: `@bind-Value` needs a `Value` parameter and an `EventCallback<int>` parameter named exactly `ValueChanged`.

checks.label: A `[Parameter] public EventCallback<int> ValueChanged`
checks.hint: Add `[Parameter] public EventCallback<int> ValueChanged { get; set; }`.

checks.label: `Value` is never assigned in the component
checks.hint: Don't change `Value`. Send the new value with `ValueChanged.InvokeAsync`.

practice.title: A bindable search box, from scratch
practice.task:
Write **`SearchBox.razor`** so a parent can use `<SearchBox @bind-Text="query" />`:

- A `string` parameter **`Text`**.
- An **`EventCallback<string>`** parameter **`TextChanged`**.
- An `<input>` that shows `Text` with **`@bind:get`**, sends new values with **`@bind:set`**, and updates on **every key**.
- The new value must reach the parent through `TextChanged` (you can pass `TextChanged` to `@bind:set` directly, or write a method that calls `TextChanged.InvokeAsync`).
practice.hint: `@bind-Text` on the parent needs `Text` and `TextChanged`. Inside, `<input @bind:get="Text" @bind:set="..." @bind:event="oninput" />`.

checks.label: A `[Parameter] public string Text` property
checks.hint: Add `[Parameter] public string Text { get; set; } = "";`.

checks.label: A `[Parameter] public EventCallback<string> TextChanged`
checks.hint: Add `[Parameter] public EventCallback<string> TextChanged { get; set; }`.

checks.label: The value goes to the parent through `TextChanged`
checks.hint: Call `await TextChanged.InvokeAsync(value);` in your set method, or write `@bind:set="TextChanged"`.

quiz.body: An input has `@bind="email"` and nothing else. When is the field `email` updated?
options: On every key the user presses
Only when the form is submitted
When the input raises `onchange`: it loses focus or the user presses Enter
Every 500 ms while the user types
quiz.explanation: For an `<input>`, `@bind` listens to **`onchange`** by default. Add `@bind:event="oninput"` to update on every key.

quiz.body: `Save` is a `void` method. What is wrong with `<button @onclick="Save()">Save</button>`?
options: It calls `Save` while rendering instead of passing it as the handler, so it doesn't build
Nothing: it's the normal way to write a handler
It works, but the page won't re-render after the click
quiz.explanation: `@onclick="Save()"` is the **result** of calling `Save`, and a `void` result can't be a handler. Pass the method group `@onclick="Save"`, or a lambda `@onclick="() => Save()"`.

quiz.body: AI code has `<input @bind="search" @onchange="Filter" />`. What happens, and what is the fix?
options: It works: `Filter` runs before the field is updated
It works: `Filter` runs after the field is updated
`Filter` never runs, but there's no error
It doesn't build because `onchange` is used twice; use `@bind:after="Filter"`
quiz.explanation: `@bind` already writes an `onchange` handler, so adding `@onchange` sets the same attribute twice, which is a **build error**. `@bind:after="Filter"` runs `Filter` after the value is stored.

quiz.body: A child calls the parent through a parameter. Which parameter type makes Blazor **re-render the parent** automatically?
quiz.explanation: When an **`EventCallback`** is invoked, Blazor runs the handler and then re-renders the component that owns it (the parent). With `Action` or `Func`, the method runs, but the parent isn't re-rendered.

quiz.body: A parent writes `<ColorPicker @bind-Color="theme" />`. What must `ColorPicker` have?
options: A `[Parameter] Color` and an `[Parameter] EventCallback<T> ColorChanged`
A `[Parameter] Color` and an `[Parameter] Action<T> OnColor`
Only a `[Parameter] Color`; Blazor tracks changes itself
quiz.explanation: `@bind-Color` expands to `Color="theme"` plus `ColorChanged="..."`. The child needs **`Color`** and an **`EventCallback<T>` named `ColorChanged`**, and calls `ColorChanged.InvokeAsync(newValue)`.

quiz.body: In `void OnPick(ChangeEventArgs e)`, what is the type of `e.Value`?
quiz.explanation: `ChangeEventArgs.Value` is an **`object?`**. Convert it, for example `e.Value?.ToString()`, or parse it for a number.

quiz.body: In which case do you really need to call `StateHasChanged()`?
options: At the end of every `@onclick` handler
When a `System.Threading.Timer` callback changes a field the component shows
In `OnInitialized`, so the first render happens
quiz.explanation: Blazor re-renders after its **own** events and when parameters are set. A timer or service event happens **outside** that, so you call `StateHasChanged()` yourself, through `InvokeAsync(StateHasChanged)` when you're on another thread.

quiz.body:
```razor
@row.Name
``` Clicking **Delete** also selects the row. How do you stop that?
quiz.explanation: The click **bubbles** from the button up to the `div`. `@onclick:stopPropagation` on the **button** stops it there. `preventDefault` only blocks the browser's default action, which a plain button doesn't have.

quiz.body: In a Blazor Web App, a page has a button with `@onclick="Increment"`. Clicking it does nothing and there's no error. What is the most likely cause?
options: The page has no interactive render mode, so it's rendered with static SSR
quiz.explanation: Without a `@rendermode` (or global interactivity), the page is **static SSR**: the HTML is sent, but no event handlers are connected. Add `@rendermode InteractiveServer` (or another interactive mode).

quiz.body: A handler is `async Task`: it sets `loading = true`, awaits an HTTP call, then sets `loading = false`. When does Blazor re-render?
options: When the handler first awaits, and again when it completes
Before the handler starts, and never after
quiz.explanation: Blazor renders when the task is **not yet complete** (at the first `await`), so `loading = true` shows, and again when the task **completes**. That's why a spinner works without `StateHasChanged()`.

interview.question: What does `@bind` do?
interview.modelAnswer: It binds a value in both directions: it writes the field into the element, and updates the field when the element raises an event. For an input, the default event is `onchange` (blur or Enter). It's a shortcut for `value` plus an `onchange` handler.

interview.question: What is the difference between `@bind` and `@bind:event="oninput"`?
interview.modelAnswer: Plain `@bind` updates the field on `onchange`, when the input loses focus. With `@bind:event="oninput"`, it updates on every key. Use `oninput` for live search or counters, and `@bind:after` to run code after each update.

interview.question: How do you make your own component work with `@bind-Value`?
interview.modelAnswer: Give it a `[Parameter] Value` and a `[Parameter] EventCallback<T> ValueChanged`. When the value should change, the component calls `ValueChanged.InvokeAsync(newValue)` instead of setting `Value`. The parent stores the new value and passes it back down.

interview.question: What is the difference between `EventCallback` and `Action` for a parameter?
interview.modelAnswer: Both let a child call the parent. `EventCallback` also re-renders the component that owns the handler, supports async handlers, and is a struct that's never null. With `Action`, the parent's method runs but its UI is not updated.

interview.question: When does a Blazor component re-render?
interview.modelAnswer: After one of its event handlers runs (and again after an async handler completes), when its parent re-renders and sets its parameters, and when `StateHasChanged()` is called. `ShouldRender()` can return false to skip renders after the first one.

interview.question: When do you need to call `StateHasChanged()`?
interview.modelAnswer: When the state changes outside Blazor's own events: a timer, a service event, a background task. From another thread, use `InvokeAsync(StateHasChanged)`. You don't need it at the end of a normal event handler.

interview.question: What do `@onclick:preventDefault` and `@onclick:stopPropagation` do?
interview.modelAnswer: `preventDefault` blocks the browser's default action, like following a link or submitting a form, while your handler still runs. `stopPropagation` stops the event from bubbling to parent elements, so their handlers don't run.

interview.question: A button's `@onclick` does nothing and there's no error. What do you check?
interview.modelAnswer: First the render mode: in a Blazor Web App, a page without an interactive render mode is static SSR, and events are not connected. Then check that the handler is passed as `Increment` or a lambda, not called as `Increment()`.
